records.reason: ChatSection renders a bare native textarea and removes only its border. UA origin explains the measured inset but does not justify excluding an input. Retain as an unresolved owner pending normalization to the shared multiline field contract or a defensible explicit exception.
Badge owns a deliberately non-Field inline inset and derives its minimum inline canvas from its painted body line. Its nested form is split into an extra record.
The summary trigger only removes the native disclosure marker and sets cursor/list styling. It owns no padding, margin or intrinsic gap.
The activated focus state owns both its visible box insets and its viewport placement. These legacy space aliases are not the shared action-row contract.
The normal, disabled and loading buttons share one border-aware Action row. The aggregate catalog ID also matches the geometry-breaking link variant, which is therefore decomposed as an extra.
The default chip owns Action insets, a component-intrinsic trailing separation, a paint floor and regular-row compensation. The host-owned nested form is an extra.
The summary owns the disclosure canvas, marker gap and group inset; this is the marker relationship within the same row separately covered by the summary-row witness.
Each non-first item owns the separator's two inline margins. The slash glyph is intrinsic paint; only its authored separation is spacing.
The submenu row owns a fixed caret canvas, the shared mark gap and automatic trailing placement; those are intrinsic to the command row.
Announcement owns its icon canvas and icon-to-copy gap independently of the frame insets covered by the frame witness.

The event composition owns the bare marker gap and its content child owns the event-to-event block separation; together they determine the occupied event row.

records.reason: The marker and connecting rail contain several component-local geometry hooks. The connector is positioned paint, but the marker canvas and top margin participate in layout.
The inner content row owns the optional icon relationship. Its gap is Field-block spacing, not the shared leading-mark gap, which is taxonomy pressure.
The summary is a regular compensated row with deliberately asymmetric inline edges; marker geometry is decomposed by the marker witness.
Menu items are the canonical continuous-fill in-box Action row: compensation is absorbed into block-end padding rather than exported as margin.
The submenu uses the identical Item renderer and contract as the root menu.
The list rail paints with an inset shadow and contributes no border or inset. Child tabs own all occupied row geometry.
A tab is an in-box Action row whose trailing compensation remains inside the block-end edge so the active bar can meet the rail.
The active selector adds paint only. It supports the invariant that active and inactive tabs keep the same Item-owned geometry.
KeyboardKeys is not a framed box: the group owns its child gap and its own inline separation, while each KeyboardKey owns the painted keycap inset.
The expanded panel composes a Continuation text-start keyline with a Surface trailing edge and the same asymmetric block edges as Card/Tile content.
The body is a real text keyline supporting the panel assignment; the component inset belongs to the parent and the paragraph's block adjustment belongs to the shared typography role.
Image is full-bleed intrinsic artwork with no padding, margin or gap. Its responsive height deliberately sets a free media phase rather than a spacing bucket.

The joined catalog headers collapse their end inset while the separately witnessed standalone headers retain the base surface end inset. Relationship 4 is scoped to the joined selector so its zero-seam evidence cannot include standalone targets.
Card.Content is a content-bearing asymmetric section region, not a control row.
Card.Footer owns the same section edges as Content plus an intrinsic wrapping child gap.
Cards is a reusable layout group and intrinsically owns its nonzero row/column gutter, so it remains a spacing owner even though its contract is layout-owned rather than a component inset bucket.
The popup surface reserves one stroke of padding while painting its edge with a negative-offset outline; it also owns its floating viewport constraint.
The submenu is the same surface renderer and owns the same reserved edge and viewport boundary.
Tile.Header is an asymmetric padded region. Unlike Card.Header, it does not collapse its end edge when Content follows.
Tile.Content owns the same asymmetric section pattern as Card.Content and the expanded Accordion panel.
Announcement is a per-edge framed box: the emphasized leading border is subtracted only from its leading Field inset, while block edges are uniform.
The outer section owns legacy Section end spacing and the payload owns an internal grid gap; its column registration remains an explicit layout boundary.
The list witness targets a deliberately reset list and list items. Category heading spacing is a separate owner and grid-column span is layout, not a component inset.
The form wrapper owns no inset or gap. It supports the Section spacing owner while its subgrid placement is an external layout boundary.
IconSection owns its icon grid's intrinsic gap and inherits the shared Section end spacing; subgrid track selection stays layout-owned.
The catalog selector resolves the bordered deep variant. Section is a vertical region contract with independently varying start/border and end spacing, not a row.
TSection reuses the .ds.section owner. Its payload registration is layout-owned, while the outer region owns default block-end spacing.

taxonomyPressure: GLOBAL exposes compensated rows, in-box compensation placement and asymmetric container edges. These are merge-test inputs, not three established buckets: in-box compensation may be an implementation mode of one row contract, and asymmetric regions may compose compact/broad edges.

Surface-region source aliases differ: Card/Tile/Accordion use Field-gap start plus Surface end; Tooltip/Popover use Surface inline plus Field-gap block; Announcement uses Field inline plus Field-gap block. These are observed compositions to minimise, not proof of additional buckets.
Badge is block-derived paint rather than Field/Action padding, while Label remains on unrelated legacy xsmall/xxsmall aliases.

Marker relationships are not fully uniform in the reference: Tooltip maps its icon gap to spacing-gap-field-block, Chip dismiss uses a one-stroke margin, and Timeline retains local marker offset/border/rail hooks.

Section, TSection, CategoriesSection and related scaffolded components still mix component spacing with page/subgrid registration. Their grid columns/tracks are explicit layout boundaries and must not become component spacing tokens.
Rule contradicts its catalog zero-layout-paint oracle because its real height plus computed trailing margin contributes occupied flow geometry.

The catalog under-decomposes geometry-changing variants: Button link, Badge/Chip nested, standalone Card.Header, text-only Cards tracks, Section shallow/hero/deep-unbordered, and non-top Tooltip caret placements need independent part rows or explicit boundaries.
